hypotheses.statement: Tokens whose social mention velocity rises above 3 standard deviations without a matching rise in unique buyers are less likely to still have liquidity above $10k seven days later than tokens whose social and buyer velocity rise together.
hypotheses.question: Is attention without independent participation a weak survival signal?
hypotheses.population: Solana tokens first observed within 24h of launch during the study window
hypotheses.sample_definition: Tokens with at least 6h of continuous observation and at least 10 recorded social mentions
hypotheses.timeframe: detection window 6h, outcome measured at day 7
hypotheses.baseline: Tokens matched on age and launchpad whose social and buyer velocity rose together
hypotheses.expected_result: Divergent-attention tokens show a lower 7-day liquidity survival rate than the matched baseline
hypotheses.falsification_condition: Survival rates differ by less than 5 percentage points, or the difference does not hold when the sample is split by market regime

hypotheses.statement: Tokens holding top-10 holder concentration above 0.60 for more than 6 consecutive hours in their first day show a higher rate of liquidity withdrawal within 48h than tokens below that threshold.
hypotheses.question: Does sustained early concentration precede liquidity withdrawal?
hypotheses.sample_definition: Tokens with at least 6 concentration measurements in the first day
hypotheses.expected_result: Higher withdrawal rate in the concentrated group
hypotheses.falsification_condition: Withdrawal rates are within 3 percentage points, or the effect disappears when controlling for initial liquidity

experiments.title: Attention/participation divergence vs 7-day liquidity survival
experiments.method: Matched-cohort comparison. Tokens are labelled divergent when social velocity z-score exceeds 3 while unique-buyer velocity z-score stays below 1. Each divergent token is matched to a control on age bucket and launchpad. Survival is liquidity >= $10k at detection + 7 days. Significance by two-proportion z-test, then re-run split by market regime.
experiments.limitations: Demo fixture sample. 96 tokens is far below the size needed to split by market regime; the regime split leaves fewer than 30 tokens per cell.

results.summary: The pooled difference in 7-day survival was 6 percentage points in the expected direction, but it did not survive the market-regime split: in the second regime the sign reversed. The pre-registered falsification condition was met, so the hypothesis is rejected.
results.critic_notes: Sample size is insufficient for a subgroup analysis, and the divergence label was constructed from the same window used to detect the original anomaly. Result is reported as REJECTED per the falsification rule, but the underlying question remains open with a proper sample.
results.limitations: Fixture data. Not evidence about any real token.
